title: Before you add pyramid training to your workout, understand what you’re trying to achieve. 🏋️‍♂️
hook: Before you add pyramid training to your workout, understand what you’re trying to achieve. 🏋️‍♂️
caption:
Before you add pyramid training to your workout, understand what you’re trying to achieve. 🏋️‍♂️

Pyramid training is a way to organize your sets. not a shortcut to faster gains.

Here’s the lesson 👇

🔺 Ascending pyramid
Increase the weight as you reduce the reps.
Example: 12 reps → 10 reps → 8 reps.

🔻 Reverse pyramid
Start with your heaviest working set, then reduce the weight as your rep target increases.
Example: 6 reps → 8 reps → 10 reps.

title: Not sure what to charge? Here's the one test I always come back to.
hook: Not sure what to charge? Here's the one test I always come back to.
caption:
Not sure what to charge? Here's the one test I always come back to.

Charge as high as you can say with a heart in integrity and a straight face.

If you can't say it yet, drop your price until you feel good about it. Get results, then raise it until you find your sweet spot.

The biggest thing is declaring and claiming and owning your value, even past the price point that used to terrify you.

title: A method many trainers use is called double progression 💪
hook: A method many trainers use is called double progression 💪
caption:
A method many trainers use is called double progression 💪

Pick a rep range, like 8 to 12. Start with a weight you can lift for 8 good reps. Each session, aim to add a rep. Once you can hit 12 reps across all your sets with solid form, increase the weight and start back at 8.

To see your effort, trainers use "reps in reserve". That means how many more reps you could have done at the end of a set. For most sets, finishing with 1 to 3 reps left in the tank is the sweet spot 🎯

Track every session in a training log so you're working towards a clear target, not guessing 📝
